requirement:
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:

> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.

Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation in `requirements.references.util` has code and a test.

**1. Provide the built-in `habeas:util` with the stated text.**
- `src/builtins.rs` `BUILTINS` registers `habeas:util` with `roles: &[ReferenceKind::Cite]`.
- `Builtin::text` takes the text from the block quote of `:::{req} util` in `md/requirements/references.md`. `quoted_text` joins the quote lines into one paragraph.
- The unit test `habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations` asserts the start and end of the text. It also asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md`.
- `validate_references` in `src/evidence.rs` resolves built-in names alongside project definitions.

**2. Only `{cite}` may reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary.**
- This is a MAY, so nothing is required. The permitted role is still enforced.
- `Builtin::check` rejects any role other than `{cite}` with "built-in habeas:util may only be referenced with {cite}". `validate_references` reports that error.
- The unit test asserts `{impl}` and `{test}` are rejected.
- The integration test `habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review` in `tests/references.rs` checks inline, fenced with commentary, and bare fenced citations. It also checks that the `{impl}` and `{test}` citations produce errors at lines 17 and 20.

**3. An item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` must not need a citation review.**
- `citation_items` in `src/citations.rs` ends with `items.retain(...)`. That keeps only items with at least one citation whose name is not `habeas:util`.
- `validate`, `delete_orphaned_reviews`, `subject_is_current`, `select_subjects` and `disagreements` all use `citation_items`, so the exemption applies to them too.
- The integration test asserts that `inline`, `fenced` and `bare` get no "missing citation review". It asserts that `mixed`, which also cites `rules.ready`, still does.

**4. A `habeas:util` citation must cover its item under `rust_item_coverage`.**
- `unreferenced_items` in `src/rust_coverage.rs` has a `counts` closure. For a built-in name it returns `builtin.check(kind).is_ok()`, so a `{cite}` of `habeas:util` counts and other roles do not.
- It covers both inline comments and closed fences, via `outline.comments` and `comment_fences`.
- The integration test asserts that no "function inline/fenced/bare" is uncovered. It asserts that `implemented` and `tested` are uncovered, because those roles are not permitted.

No obligation is untested, and no reachable code behaves in a way the text does not specify.

text: :::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. The reviewer MUST assess, for each citation,
whether the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition
changes, and whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Search results are not evidence inputs under {cite}`requirements.authoring.text_search`, so only sources an assessment received as mandatory inputs or read count. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every uncovered item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
